reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a no-cost, risk-free method for earning limitless ETH. It directs viewers to run externally linked code, connect MetaMask, select wallet accounts, and transfer ETH to increase liquidity and supposedly generate returns. The tutorial and claimed demonstration do not verify the code, wallet permissions, contract behavior, or whether the displayed profits were obtainable.

citations.quote: The next step is to freely deploy an embedded Liquid smart contract within the Ethereum blockchain transaction pool.
To do this, enter the address of your second account into the input field and click attach.
The more Ethereum you have confirmed on your second Metamask account, the more transactions you can confirm, increasing your earnings automatically.
Click on the liquid button and start your profit, And now we can see that the Ethereum profits begin accruing.
The Withdraw all Profit button starts the process of transferring earnings to the specified Ethereum account?

opening.argument: Judge the explanation of custody alongside the earnings claims. The speaker says the ETH moves between the viewer's own accounts and remains under the viewer's control, and acknowledges that transaction fees reduce the amount received. Those statements do not prove the method works, but they matter when assessing whether the video is asking viewers to surrender funds to someone else. The stronger reading is an overly confident explanation of a wallet operation, not an established attempt to take viewers' ETH.

citations.quote: Please note, Ethereum moves between your accounts and remains under your control.
The profit received is slightly less due to the transaction fee.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening is right that the code and permissions are not verified. But that uncertainty cannot, by itself, establish that the transfer goes to an outside recipient: the speaker describes a transfer between the viewer's main and second accounts. The claimed rising earnings also deserve skepticism, yet the cited button instruction establishes what the presenter says to click, not what the code actually does.

citations.quote: Between your Main account, which holds Ethereum, and the newly created second account.
Click on the liquid button and start your profit, And now we can see that the Ethereum profits begin accruing.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the transfer controlled does not verify custody or the code. The speaker gives an unqualified assurance of limitless, risk-free earnings while directing viewers to use source code and connect MetaMask. Acknowledging a transaction fee is not a meaningful warning about the risks of the proposed contract workflow.

opening.argument: This is presented as a walkthrough of a tool and wallet workflow. The speaker gives steps for creating a second MetaMask account, deploying and attaching a contract, and inspecting a transaction in a blockchain explorer. The sampled screen also shows a code editor beside the running interface. A judge can question the profit explanation without treating every demonstrated action as proof of a deceptive solicitation; the material substantially consists of showing how the claimed setup operates.

citations.quote: Next select Add a new account and enter the desired account name such as Account2 and click create.
To do this, simply click the deploy button and wait for a short while
let's follow the link to the transaction and check the final status on the Ethereum blockchain Explorer.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the unverified code and displayed profit as decisive, but lack of verification also limits what can be concluded from the demonstration. The speaker walks through a claimed withdrawal and tells viewers to inspect the completed transaction. That does not independently establish the origin of any funds, but it is relevant context for why the video reads as a demonstration rather than merely an unsupported earnings pitch.

citations.quote: Copy it, paste it and click the withdraw all profit button.
Now let's take a look at the completed transaction. Go back to the blocks explorer.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A step-by-step format does not make the purpose educational. The instructions culminate in confirming ETH liquidity, activating supposed automatic profit, and encouraging viewers to run the linked code themselves. A successful transaction display does not establish that the promised returns come from transaction processing or that the workflow is safe.

opening.argument: The concrete links in the description point viewers to a wallet download, source code, and a place to run it; the described setup uses the viewer's own MetaMask accounts. There is no stated purchase price or instruction in those steps to send ETH to the presenter. The absence of those elements does not certify the code, but it matters: the visible offer can be read as promotion of a self-run tool rather than a request to deposit into a service controlled by the speaker.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening highlights a real concern: the linked code and wallet permissions have not been verified. Still, deploying a contract and attaching an account address do not, on their own, show a payment to the presenter. The speaker explicitly characterizes the proposed ETH movement as between the viewer's accounts. The unresolved code behavior warrants caution, but the cited instructions alone do not establish diversion of funds.

citations.quote: To do this, enter the address of your second account into the input field and click attach.
Please note, Ethereum moves between your accounts and remains under your control.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A missing purchase price or named deposit address does not resolve this concern. The viewer is directed to run externally linked code, connect a wallet, and confirm ETH liquidity in a contract workflow advertised as producing automatic returns. Whether the speaker receives funds directly is not the only relevant mechanism; the defense cannot verify what the code or approvals do.
